rules_evaluated.evidence: Chunk 5 'Freedom to choose', line 34, final bullet: 'All modules are designed to cope with missing details from prior modules.' The four preceding bullets in this section (lines 30-33) are all direct instructions to the reader (set the pace, cut depth, prioritize exercises, protect working memory); this fifth bullet breaks that pattern to comment on the CURRICULUM'S OWN construction ('are designed to cope with...') -- class (b), self-referential design commentary, the shape check_slides.md §16(b) names ('the curriculum telling the student they are inside a pedagogy'). Checked the maintainer block for a covering accept-note first: none of the eight dated notes (L88-112) attests this specific bullet. Counter-consideration weighed: the line does supply some reassurance value (permission to have gaps), which is closer to a 'tell' than idle narration -- but the section's actual permission-granting work is already complete by line 33 ('Cut where needed'), so this line's distinct contribution is specifically the claim of deliberate design, not a new move/object/tell/priority the section otherwise lacks. Non-blocking: the section is fully followable and actionable without it.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Cut the bullet, or reframe without the self-referential design claim -- e.g. fold the reassurance into the 'Protect your working memory' bullet ('Cut where needed; missing a detail from an earlier module won't strand you') so it reads as advice to the student rather than commentary on the curriculum's own construction.
